contextViews.text: I would keep reading. That is not quite the same as knowing which opening to choose.

choices.label: Begin with the woman at the door.
Keep the claim; make it less defensive.

contextViews.text: Read the story first. Then show me the sentence where curiosity has to become an argument.
She reads without looking up. At the locked door she pauses, crosses out an adjective, and continues into the evidence. You wait until she reaches the end.
There. That transition works. I was defending the whole paragraph because I liked one sentence. An extremely scholarly method.
Better. Not finished. I wanted you to like it, and then I got annoyed because that mattered so much.
I like listening to you. Sometimes I am still going to prefer the other paragraph.
I suppose I can survive questionable taste. You have survived mine in music.
She gathers both drafts into her folder rather than throwing either away. At the library door she stays beside you for another moment.
Next time, something we do not have to improve. I would like that.
In the courtyard, Boglárka takes a folded page from her bag, then puts it away before you can read it.
Still a draft. I keep improving the opening instead of letting anyone reject the rest. It is a remarkably efficient way not to finish.
I can invent a reason to delay almost anything. Usually it sounds very responsible.
Then I will try not to do it with this. With us, I mean. I want a relationship with you. Not just meetings I can explain away as something else.
I do not want you to have to bring a page every time you want to see me.
Good. Some days I am going to be poor company. And I will still want you there. If we choose a shared relationship, I am not asking for a secret promise that excludes someone else.
What do you want, Álex $& {playerName}?
I hoped for a different answer. I would rather know, though.
You stay long enough to say goodbye properly. Boglárka takes her bag toward the east passage; you leave the courtyard separately.

method: Scripted public JSON CLI, fresh saves, latest revision per action, per-node EN/HU switching, process restart, no author mode/save manipulation. No optional gatherings/preparation. One latest-window run cannot fit commitment and is intentionally unresolved.

observed.text: Boglárka has put a closed book on the courtyard bench. She moves it onto her lap when I arrive, leaving room for me.
I brought a poem to start with. Then I realised I was making somebody else ask you out.
I might have mistaken it for homework. This is much better.
Then let me be quite clear, CLI route tester. I want this to be a date.
The book is mine. An excellent alibi. I haven't managed to read a word of it.
I nearly brought notes. Fortunately I couldn't decide on a heading.
I sit at the other end of the bench. She waits, one finger still marking a page she hasn't read.
She puts the book away. A folded slip of paper escapes; she catches it and smiles at what she has written.
Thinking. But about something much less dignified than you probably imagine.
Now you have to tell me.
I wrote down a song to play you. Then three alternatives, in case you disliked the first. An entire emergency programme.
Here. The first one. You can tell me if you hate it. I'd rather have an argument than watch you being politely moved.
She plays a short piece from her phone, quietly enough for the two of us. Her foot keeps the beat. At the chorus she almost sings, then catches my eye.
The recording stops. She leaves the phone in her hand, waiting for my actual answer.
Exactly. It would be a worse song if she sang it properly. Don't tell anyone I said that about doing something properly.
I'd like to kiss you. I've been trying to find a graceful point to say it, but the drummer has rather ruined that.
I lean towards her. She meets me with a brief kiss, then sits back, still smiling. Her phone is safely in her lap.
There. I was afraid I'd spend the entire date deciding where to put that sentence.
The window alcove in the library is free. We could sit there a little longer. I want to hear your choice, too.
We go into the library and take the two chairs by the window. Her book stays in her bag; she sets her phone between us.
Here. Nobody comes to this corner unless they want to stay. It's my favourite thing about it.
She turns her chair a little towards mine. There is time for another song, or another subject.
Yes. I was hoping you would.
This time she reaches me first. We kiss, and she laughs softly against my cheek before moving back to her chair.
I like having somewhere to come back to. I mean this corner. Also this.
We put our phones away and leave the library together. Outside, she adjusts her bag and walks with me towards the gate.
I'd like to do this again. I can bring something considerably worse to listen to.
I'd like that. Including the part where you nearly sing.
“I might, next time.” She says goodbye at the gate. I watch her go a little way before turning towards my own door.
Egy megbeszélésen Márton Boglárka helyett fejezett be egy magyarázatot. A könyvtárban Boglárka nem ül le rögtön.
Segíteni akartál, de mindenki megint téged hallott. Veled sem szeretnék lábjegyzet lenni.
Láttam, hogy tudod, mire gondolok. Még örültem is. Aztán már te mondtad, én meg ott álltam melletted.
Azt hittem, megkönnyítem, ha sürgetnek.
Nehéz volt. De el akartam mondani. Most neked köszönték meg, én meg megint majdnem csatlakoztam hozzájuk.
Szeretném megérteni, mi történt köztünk, mielőtt válaszolok.
A következő alkalommal várd ki a mondatomat. Akkor is, ha túl lassúnak tartasz.
Nem szeretném egy bocsánatkéréssel elintézni.
Hogyan kezdjük újra ezt a beszélgetést?
Azt fogom mondani, hogy még nem fejeztem be. Nem titkos jel kell hozzá.
Akkor megállok. Nem kell megindokolnod.
És ha nem kérek segítséget, attól még lehet nehéz. A kettőt szeretném én különválasztani.
Márton megírja a helyesbítést. Boglárka egy mondatot kihúz, a saját megfogalmazását írja a helyére; ez a változat megy a csoportnak.
Nem attól leszünk közel, hogy mindig ugyanarra jutunk. Legközelebb lehet, hogy vitatkozom is veled.
Szeretném végighallgatni.
A csendes udvaron most nem a következő veszélyről beszéltek. A korábbi jóvátételnek azóta is érvényt kellett szerezni.
A megbeszélésen tegnap nem segítettél ki. Észrevetted, milyen sokáig kerestem azt a szót?
Igen.
Én meg azt, hogy kivártad. Utána már azt is ki mertem mondani, amiben nem értettem egyet veled. Jó volt úgy kijönni, hogy nem kellett visszamennem a saját mondatomért.
A saját szavaimmal mondom: kapcsolatot szeretnék veled, nem meg nem nevezett mellékszálat valaki életében.
Nem ígérek olyat, amit más helyett kellene eldöntenem.
Én ezt választom. Szeretnék helyet az életedben, amiről beszélhetünk, akkor is, ha nem értünk egyet.
A vállalásomhoz a saját időmből és a kényelmes titkolózásból is engednem kell.
Mit szeretnél a következő találkozón?
Az első számot én választom. Még mindig nincs hozzá szövegelemzés.
A második az enyém. Lehet, hogy nem fog tetszeni.
Akkor végre kölcsönös lesz a kockázat.
Elküldtem a tanulmányt. Utána tíz percig néztem az elküldött üzenetet. A nevem ott volt. Aztán még mindig ott volt.
Örülök.
Én is. Most már nem kell újraolvasnom, hogy biztos legyek benne.
After the institutional meeting I find Boglárka by the courtyard bench. She is staring at her phone. When she sees me, she turns the screen my way.
Submission received. That's all it says. I've read it enough times to have a strong opinion about the punctuation.
You sent it. With your name on it.
Yes. Not accepted, not published. Sent. I keep trying to skip to knowing whether they like it.
I wish there were a receipt for the rest of this year. Something that said we'd finished with it.
I don't think I'd believe it. I still stop when I hear a door shut below us. But I don't want every time I see you to be about that door.
I want to keep seeing you, CLI route tester. With things to tell you that haven't happened yet.
Her thumb rests on the edge of the screen. I sit on the other end of the bench before I answer.
She turns the phone face down between us. For a moment we watch a leaf travel along a crack in the paving.
Our music evening. Yes. I still have the list. I've added something you might actually like; it felt rather reckless.
I left the books at home. I'd like a little more time with you. We could stay here, or go up to your suite.
We walk to my suite. I put my keys on the desk and move a pile of papers off the spare chair. She takes it, setting her bag beside her feet.
So this is where all the unfinished sentences live. I feel quite at home.
She looks up at me, amused. I leave the papers where they are.
Yes. Come here.
I move closer. She stands to meet me, resting a hand on my shoulder as we kiss. When we draw apart she keeps looking at me.
I'd like to stay with you, properly alone. Not just for another song.
I want that too.
She sets her phone beside mine and takes my hand. We leave the chairs behind. The rest of our time together stays private.
Later, she reaches for the glass of water on my desk. I almost start apologising for the papers. She raises an eyebrow before I can.
Leave them. I like knowing you don't finish everything either.
We gather the phones. Boglárka lifts her bag, and I walk her to my door. She says she'd like to bring the next song herself.
We say goodbye. Her steps recede along the corridor; I go back inside and leave the papers until later.

outcome.viragText: A Mérceháló év végi cikksorozatában Virág feltárja a visszatartott ösztöndíjak, a valótlan felújítási teljesítések és az elhallgatott panaszok ügyét. A pénzeket kiutalják, a hibás teljesítést visszavonják, a felelős vezetőt leváltják. Riporteri nyomozása sikeresen lezárul; a hatósági utóeljárás folytatódik.
outcome.institutionText: A főiskola részleges tájékoztatást ad. A sérült vagy visszatartott bizonyítékok miatt több kérdés nyitva marad.
outcome.relationshipText: A visszalépést tiszteletben tartották. A közös nyomozás megmarad, a magánéleti találkozások elmaradnak. Senki nem tartozik érzelmekkel azért, mert segítséget kapott.
outcome.threatText: A vámpír meghalt a megszakított átalakulásban. A segítők megállították a rítust, de a csoport súlyosan kimerült, és iratok sérültek meg. Lilla és a többiek fokozatosan épülnek fel; az emlékek nem térnek vissza egyszerre.
